first_impression.reaction: My daughter sent this so I'd stop asking what needs doing when. It's sensible and calm, no silly slang, and it's set out in short lists, which suits the iPad. I liked that it puts money and who is paying first, in writing. The passport and insurance points are exactly what I'd have nagged about. What it doesn't do is say a word about deposits being safe, or how Mum gets around if she can't manage steps.

journey.quote: A year sounds like a long time until you count the things that cannot be rushed: a venue on your date, a gown made to measure, a passport renewal, legal papers for marrying overseas.
journey.reaction: Quite right. Nobody my daughter's age thinks about passports until the week before.

journey.section: 12 months out: what to do first
journey.quote: Agree what you will spend and who is contributing, in writing between the two of you, before any venue conversation.
journey.reaction: Good. Though it's not just the two of them. Their father and I are paying half, so we should be in that conversation too.

journey.section: 12 months out: what to do first
journey.quote: Take out travel insurance as soon as you book the site visit or flights.
journey.reaction: Practical. That's the sort of thing a responsible company says.

journey.section: 10 to 11 months out: book the people who shape the day
journey.quote: Hold a block of rooms for guests close to the venue, with a release date agreed in writing.
journey.reaction: In writing again. I like that. But who pays if the rooms aren't filled?

journey.section: 8 to 9 months out: attire, accommodation and the celebrant
journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor is the one person who plans with you from start to finish, works in your time zone and agrees the fee in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: This is the line I'll forward to my husband. One person, our time zone, fee in writing. Now give me a name and a phone number.

journey.section: 6 to 7 months out: rings, stationery and the details
journey.quote: When you buy travel insurance, declare everything upfront, including all pre-existing health conditions, or you may void the policy.
journey.reaction: Very important for Mum and my brother-in-law with his heart. I'm glad it says it plainly.

journey.section: 1 month out: the final legal and supplier check
journey.quote: Pay outstanding balances on the dates in each contract.
journey.reaction: That's the only mention of contracts and money in the whole list. What about the deposits paid eleven months earlier to people overseas? Are they protected? Whose contract is it?

journey.quote: Send guests a short travel note: transfer times, the welcome event and who to call on arrival.
journey.reaction: Who to call, yes. But who do we call at 2am if something goes wrong? Is that Wedded Wonderland or the venue?

journey.quote: Arrive with time to settle, and walk the venue at the hour of the ceremony.
journey.reaction: Nowhere in the whole year does it say check that older guests can actually get to the ceremony spot. My mother uses a walking frame. That should be on a checklist.

journey.section: Plan the year with one person beside you
journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor helps you decide it, as your single point of contact from the first idea, quoting in AUD and confirming inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: AUD quotes and things in writing before we commit. That settles a lot of my worries about currency and contracts.

unanswered_questions: Are deposits paid to overseas venues and suppliers protected, and who holds the contract: us, the venue or Wedded Wonderland? (deferred business detail)
Who do we ring on the day, or at 2am local time, if something goes wrong, and is anyone from Wedded Wonderland there? (deferred business detail)
Can a parent who is paying join the first conversation, and is it a phone call with a named person?
Does the Wedded Advisor check step-free access and transfers for elderly or less mobile guests?
If the room block isn't filled by the release date, who is liable for the empty rooms?

turn_offs_found.quote: Pay outstanding balances on the dates in each contract.
turn_offs_found.why: It is the only line about contracts and payments in a twelve-month plan. Nothing about deposits, whether they are protected or who is responsible if an overseas supplier fails. That is exactly what I'd be worried about.

would_share_with: My husband, the 'agrees the fee in writing before any work begins' line, with my question about deposits
My daughter, the insurance line about declaring pre-existing conditions, for the older guests
My sister, the passport section, because hers expires next year

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, talk to Wedded Concierge about your date and destination.
cta_reaction.why: It's polite and not pushy, and AUD quotes in writing reassure me. But I'd want a phone call with a named person first, and answers on deposits and who we ring on the day, before I let my daughter book anything.

top_3_changes: Add a line, early in the plan, on how deposits to overseas suppliers are handled and who holds the contract, only if the business confirms it; otherwise flag.
Add an accessibility task (step-free route, transfers and seating for older or less mobile guests) to the destination track, for example at the site visit or the week of.
In the 12 months out block, mention that parents or anyone contributing should be part of the written spend agreement, not only the couple.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Margaret (funding parent): read top to bottom on iPad, focused on money, accountability, older guests and a phone call
No invented brand facts; deposits, on-the-day contact and accessibility placed in unanswered_questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (fact tags, image slots) ignored

open_questions.question: Can the business confirm how overseas deposits and the on-the-day contact are handled, so one line can be added? If not, flag rather than fill. Also consider an accessibility task for older guests in the destination track.

assumptions: Margaret arrived via a link from her daughter, reading on an iPad, as a parent contributing about half.
Relevance is moderate: the checklist is the couple's job, but money, insurance and passports are her concerns.
Fast mode: full article read top to bottom; the CTA quote is the visible link text in the closing paragraph.
